questions: Does your muscle weakness worsen with activity and improve after rest?
Do you have double vision?
Do either of your eyelids droop, especially later in the day?
Do you have difficulty keeping your eyes open when tired?
Do you have difficulty chewing or swallowing?
Does your speech become softer, slurred, or nasal when you talk for a while?
Do you ever choke on food, liquids, or saliva?
Do you have difficulty holding your head up?
Do you have weakness in your arms or hands?
Do you have difficulty climbing stairs or rising from a chair?
Have you noticed worsening weakness in your feet or difficulty lifting the front of either foot?
Do you have numbness, tingling, or reduced sensation in your feet?
Have these symptoms been progressively worsening?
Did the symptoms begin suddenly?
Have you had shortness of breath when lying down or during ordinary activity?
Has anyone in your family had similar weakness or difficulty walking?
Do you have diabetes, thyroid disease, or another autoimmune disease?
Have you recently started any medication or had a medication dose increased?
Have you ever had surgery or imaging showing a mass in your chest?
Have you previously been diagnosed with a neuromuscular disorder?

results: 1. Comprehensive neurologic examination, including ocular alignment and extraocular movements, fatigability, facial strength, limb strength, reflexes, plantar responses, sensation, coordination, and gait (including heel and toe walking)
cranial nerve examination: bilateral abduction limitation, worse on the right, with diplopia in all directions
limb strength (MRC) examination: mild distal limb weakness
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: reduced or absent reflexes; flexor plantar responses
sensory examination (pinprick, vibration, proprioception): distal loss of vibration and proprioception
coordination examination (limb and truncal): normal
sustained upgaze fatigability test: no fatigable droop
ocular motility examination: bilateral limitation of abduction, worse on the right, with diplopia in all directions
cover test / ocular alignment: orthophoric
2. Nerve conduction studies and needle electromyography
nerve conduction studies: demyelinating sensorimotor neuropathy
needle electromyography: chronic neurogenic changes
3. MRI of the brain and orbits with contrast
MRI orbits: normal extraocular muscles, no mass
MRI brain with contrast: bilateral contrast enhancement and THICKENING of cranial nerves III through XII
4. Serum creatine kinase
creatine kinase: normal
creatine kinase and lactate: normal
5. Serum TSH and free T4
thyroid function (TSH, free T4): normal
TSH / free T4 / TRAb: normal, TRAb negative
6. Serum vitamin B12, methylmalonic acid, and copper
vitamin B12 with methylmalonic acid: normal
serum copper and caeruloplasmin: normal
7. Serum glucose and HbA1c
blood glucose and HbA1c: normal
glucose / HbA1c: normal
8. Serum acetylcholine-receptor and MuSK antibodies
acetylcholine receptor, MuSK and LRP4 antibodies: normal
anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies: negative
anti-MuSK antibodies: negative
9. Repetitive nerve stimulation and single-fiber electromyography
repetitive nerve stimulation: normal
single-fibre EMG: normal jitter
10. Comprehensive hereditary motor neuropathy and neuromuscular disease genetic panel, including PMP22 copy-number analysis and mitochondrial DNA testing
mitochondrial genetics (mtDNA deletion): no deletion
whole exome sequencing: heterozygous likely pathogenic FBLN5 c.1117C>T (p.Arg373Cys) - CMT1H
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Charcot–Marie–Tooth disease type 1H (FBLN5-related hereditary demyelinating sensorimotor neuropathy) due to the heterozygous likely pathogenic FBLN5 c.1117C>T (p.Arg373Cys) variant, with hypertrophic cranial neuropathy causing bilateral ophthalmoplegia

ALTERNATIVE: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy with cranial-nerve involvement

ALTERNATIVE: MADSAM/Lewis–Sumner variant of CIDP

ALTERNATIVE: Infectious or inflammatory hypertrophic multiple cranial neuropathy (for example, neurosarcoidosis)
